title: Heron Post
shortDescription: A fishing post and a whistle that should have been heard.
longDescription:
A post stands in the shallows where a heron might fish and a lookout might not. Heron Midge is the lookout, tall and grey and tired of other people's boats.
North is the rope-island. East is the pirate camp.

fixtures.name: Heron Midge
fixtures.lookDescription: A tall grey heron in a fisherman's vest, spear grounded, not raised. Try talk midge.
fixtures.examineDescription: Midge's vest is patched with oilcloth. The spear is for fish. She has stood this post through floods and through thieves, and she hates both for the same reason: they take the river's manners.
fixtures.dialogue: Midge stands on one leg in the shallows with her spear grounded, and she does not shift when you come up the bank. "Nett will have told you about tins. I will tell you about the nail." She looks at the post beside her, where the nail is bright and empty. "I hung a whistle there eleven years ago, so anybody cutting a rope downstream would be heard doing it. Somebody took the whistle and left the nail. That is a different crime than stealing a boat, and a worse one. Talk midge."

fixtures.name: Whistle Post
fixtures.lookDescription: A post with a nail where a whistle hung. Examine it.
fixtures.examineDescription: The nail is bright. The whistle is gone. Midge says she hung it so the landing would hear a cut painter. Someone kept the whistle instead of the warning.
